key_insight: This paper shows that LLMs used for code vulnerability detection may be influenced by cognitive heuristics, not just the actual security flaws in code. The authors introduce the first systematic framework to study these biases in LLM-based vulnerability assessment.
problem_solved: It addresses the lack of understanding about whether and how human-like cognitive heuristics distort LLM judgments when detecting code vulnerabilities.
method: Built a controlled experimental framework to test heuristic effects in LLM vulnerability detection.
Systematically varied code and context signals to isolate when model decisions are driven by heuristics rather than true security evidence.
Compared LLM assessments across conditions to identify bias patterns in vulnerability predictions.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work highlights that LLM security tools can be biased by superficial cues, which may lead to false alarms or missed vulnerabilities. It suggests the need for more robust evaluation and safer deployment of LLM-based security scanners.
visual_elements: Split-screen diagram showing true vulnerability evidence vs heuristic-driven cues
Flowchart of the controlled experimental framework
Bar chart comparing LLM accuracy across different heuristic conditions
Icons representing common heuristics such as authority, wording, and framing
paper_title: Words Speak Louder Than Code: Investigating Cognitive Heuristics in LLM-Based Code Vulnerability Detection
paper_authors: Asif Shahriar, Hongyu Cai, Hadjer Benkraouda, Gang Wang, Z. Berkay Celik
